name: End table
spec: Wood-effect chipboard · built from a 2-page paper manual · sizes estimated

steps.title: Screw mini fix bolts into the top
steps.text: Lay top panel A unfinished side up. Screw the four mini fix bolts (5) into the pre-drilled holes with a screwdriver.

steps.title: Fit caps, dowels and nail legs to the sides
steps.text: On each side panel C, press in two mini fix caps (4) with the arrows pointing outward, then tap two dowels (2) into the top edge and two nail legs (3) into the bottom edge with a hammer.

steps.title: Lay out the left side panel
steps.text: Stand the left side panel C on its back edge with its hardware facing in.

steps.title: Fit both shelf panels
steps.text: Hold both shelf panels B against the left side panel, lined up with the screw holes and unfinished surfaces as shown.

steps.title: Screw the shelves to the left side
steps.text: Drive four chipboard screws (1) through the left side panel into the shelf ends with a screwdriver.

steps.title: Fit the right side panel
steps.text: Place the right side panel C against the other ends of both shelves, hardware facing in.

steps.title: Screw the right side
steps.text: Drive four chipboard screws (1) through the right side panel into the shelves with a screwdriver.

steps.title: Stand the unit upright
steps.text: Turn the unit up so it stands on its nail legs.

steps.title: Fit the top and lock the caps
steps.text: Lower top panel A so its bolts and the dowels drop into the side panels. Turn each mini fix cap (4) with a screwdriver to lock the top.

steps.title: Slide in the bin
steps.text: Unfold the non-woven bin (6), fit its base board, and slide it into the space above the middle shelf.

notes: All sizes are estimates for a small end table: top 40 x 40 x 1.5 cm, sides 46.2 x 34 x 1.2 cm, shelves 33.6 x 33 x 1.2 cm, overall height about 48 cm.
The top panel is drawn as a plain box; the manual shows rounded corners.
The finish is not given in the line-drawing manual; a dark wood-effect colour was chosen.
The manual shows steps 3 and 4 with the side panels standing on a long edge, so the build starts lying on its back. It could equally be lying on its front.
Shelf heights are estimated from the drawings: bottom shelf about 4.4 cm up, middle shelf about 31.9 cm up, leaving about 13 cm for the bin.
The shelves are joined to the sides with screws only, two per shelf end.
Step 2 shows one side panel with x2 quantities of each fitting; the same is done to both side panels, which uses all 4 caps, 4 dowels and 4 nail legs.
The positions of the mini fix caps, dowels and nail legs along the panel edges are estimated.
The mini fix bolts are drawn with their head end down in the cam and their thread in the top panel. Their length and the cap depth are reduced so nothing passes through the 1.2 cm side panels.
Dowel length is shortened to 2.4 cm so it does not poke through the 1.5 cm top.
The nail leg heads rest on the floor at y = 0, with the side panels sitting just above them.
Locking the mini fix caps in step 5 is folded into the top-panel step, because the caps were already placed in step 2.
The non-woven bin is drawn as a single box. Unfolding it and inserting its base board are only described in the text.
The manual has no wall-fixing step.
